newsitem.title: USA: U.S. securities group says laws need broad update.
newsitem.headline: U.S. securities group says laws need broad update.

text.p: The Securities Industry Association (SIA), a trade group for brokers and investment banking firms, said it supports a comprehensive overhaul of depression-era industry regulations, rather than what it called the "piecemeal" approach of the Federal Reserve Board.
The group issued the statement folowing a decision by the Federal Reserve Wednesday easing some restrictions on securities affiliates of banks.

"SIA believes that comprehensive modernization of the laws governing the financial services industry by Congress is the only means by which banks and securities firms (as well as insurance companies and other financial services providers) will be able to compete and affiliate on a fair and rational basis," SIA senior vice president for government affairs Steve Judge said in a statement.
Judge said the Fed's actions "are not long-term solutions to the complicated competitive issues caused by the now-antiquated statutes regulating the financial services industry."

In its action Wednesday, the Fed permitted banks to share employees between a bank and its securities affiliate; cross-sell products of the securities subsidiary; and buy and sell for its own account a broader range of securities in transactions with the securities affiliate.

"There is no compelling need for the FRB at this time to take piecemeal action such as eliminating firewalls that could jeopardize prospects for enhancing comprehensive financial services modernization legislation in the next Congress," Judge said.

He said the SIA suports consistent rules through a pollicy of functional regulation and a competitive arena in which banks can own full service securities firms and securities firms can own or affiliate with banks.
